fr.B: Le commandant de la garde emporta les gobelets, les brasiers, les bassins à aspersion, les pots, les chandeliers, les coupes et les vases à libations, tout ce qui était en or et tout ce qui était en argent.
fr.R: Le chef de la garde a aussi pris les gobelets, les brasiers, les bassins pour l’aspersion, les pots, les chandeliers, les coupes et les vases qui servaient aux offrandes de vin. Il a pris tout ce qui était en or et tout ce qui était en argent.

sw.L: Na vikombe na vyetezo na mabakuli na masufuria na vinara na sahani na mabirika, kilichokuwa dhahabu, dhahabu, na kilichokuwa fedha, fedha, mkuu wa walinzi akavichukua.
sw.B: Kamanda wa walinzi alichukua vikombe, vyetezo, mabakuli ya kunyunyizia, masufuria, vinara, sahani na mabirika ya sadaka za kinywaji, kila kitu kilichotengenezwa kwa dhahabu na kila kitu kilichotengenezwa kwa fedha.
sw.R: Kamanda wa walinzi alichukua pia vikombe, vyetezo, mabakuli ya kunyunyizia, masufuria, vinara, sahani na mabirika yaliyotumika kwa sadaka za kinywaji. Alichukua kila kitu kilichotengenezwa kwa dhahabu na kila kitu kilichotengenezwa kwa fedha.

vi.L: Các chén, lư hương, chậu, nồi, chân đèn, đĩa và bình, thứ bằng vàng ra vàng, thứ bằng bạc ra bạc, quan chỉ huy vệ binh lấy đi.
vi.B: Quan chỉ huy đội cận vệ lấy đi các chén, lư hương, chén rảy, nồi, chân đèn, đĩa và các bình dùng cho lễ quán, mọi thứ làm bằng vàng và mọi thứ làm bằng bạc.
vi.R: Người chỉ huy đội cận vệ cũng lấy các chén, lư hương, chén rảy, nồi, chân đèn, đĩa và các bình dùng để dâng rượu. Ông lấy mọi thứ làm bằng vàng và mọi thứ làm bằng bạc.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 25:15 with a longer list
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 25:15 names only the firepans and the bowls. Jeremiah adds the cups, pots, lampstands, dishes and jugs, much as 1 Kings 7:49-50 lists the gold furnishings Solomon made.

decisions.choice: gold, gold; silver, silver: everything of gold and everything of silver
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:15, the doubled word gathers everything of that metal: whatever was gold and whatever was silver. Some take it to stress the metal, "pure gold", or to mean that these were taken for their value as metal.

decisions.choice: jugs: vessels for pouring drink offerings
decisions.reason: The word is used of the jugs on the table of the bread of the presence, "with which drink offerings are poured out" (Exodus 25:29; Numbers 4:7).

decisions.choice: lampstands: the ten lampstands of Solomon's temple
decisions.reason: Solomon had made ten gold lampstands for the temple, five on each side (1 Kings 7:49).

decisions.choice: firepans, fire pans (Readable); sprinkling bowls; jars for drink offerings (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:50, 2 Kings 25:15 and Exodus 25:29. Balanced and Readable add what the jars were for.

source.text: הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים׀שְׁנַ֗יִם הַיָּ֤ם אֶחָד֙ וְהַבָּקָ֞ר שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֤ר נְחֹ֨שֶׁת֙ אֲשֶׁר־תַּ֣חַת הַמְּכֹנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה לֹא־הָיָ֣ה מִשְׁקָ֔ל לִנְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: The pillars two, the sea one, and the bulls twelve [of] bronze which [were] under the stands, which had made the king Solomon for [the] house of Yahweh, there was no weight to their bronze, all the vessels these.

en.L: The two pillars, the one sea, and the twelve bulls of bronze that [were] under the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: there was no weight for the bronze of all these vessels.
en.B: As for the two pillars, the one Sea and the twelve bronze bulls under the stands, which King Solomon made for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the bronze of all these things was more than could be weighed.
en.R: The two pillars, the Sea, and the twelve bronze bulls under the stands, all made by King Solomon for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, held so much bronze that no one could weigh it.

es.L: Las dos columnas, el mar único, y los doce bueyes de bronce que [estaban] debajo de las basas, que el rey Salomón había hecho para la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}: no había peso para el bronce de todos estos utensilios.
es.B: En cuanto a las dos columnas, el único Mar y los doce bueyes de bronce que estaban debajo de las basas, que el rey Salomón había hecho para la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el bronce de todas estas cosas era más de lo que se podía pesar.
es.R: Las dos columnas, el Mar y los doce bueyes de bronce que estaban debajo de las basas, todo hecho por el rey Salomón para el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, tenían tanto bronce que nadie podía pesarlo.

fr.L: Les deux colonnes, la Mer unique, et les douze taureaux de bronze qui [étaient] sous les bases, que le roi Salomon avait faits pour la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} : il n’y avait pas de poids pour le bronze de tous ces objets.
fr.B: Quant aux deux colonnes, à la Mer unique et aux douze taureaux de bronze placés sous les bases, que le roi Salomon avait faits pour la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, le bronze de tous ces objets était impossible à peser.
fr.R: Les deux colonnes, la Mer et les douze taureaux de bronze placés sous les bases, que le roi Salomon avait fabriqués pour le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, contenaient tellement de bronze que personne n’aurait pu le peser.

sw.L: Nguzo mbili, bahari moja, na mafahali kumi na wawili wa shaba waliokuwa chini ya vitako, ambavyo mfalme Sulemani alivifanya kwa ajili ya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: shaba ya vyombo hivi vyote haikuwa na uzito [uliopimika].
sw.B: Kuhusu nguzo mbili, Bahari moja na mafahali kumi na wawili wa shaba waliokuwa chini ya vitako, ambavyo mfalme Sulemani alivifanya kwa ajili ya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, shaba ya vitu hivyo vyote ilikuwa nyingi mno kupimwa.
sw.R: Nguzo mbili, Bahari, na mafahali kumi na wawili wa shaba waliokuwa chini ya vitako, vyote vilivyotengenezwa na mfalme Sulemani kwa ajili ya hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, vilikuwa na shaba nyingi mno hata hakuna mtu aliyeweza kuipima.

vi.L: Hai cây trụ, một cái biển, và mười hai con bò bằng đồng ở dưới các chân đế, mà vua Sa-lô-môn đã làm cho nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: đồng của mọi khí cụ ấy không thể cân được.
vi.B: Còn hai cây trụ, một cái Biển và mười hai con bò bằng đồng ở dưới các chân đế, mà vua Sa-lô-môn đã làm cho nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, thì đồng của tất cả các vật ấy nhiều không cân xuể.
vi.R: Hai cây trụ, cái Biển, và mười hai con bò bằng đồng dưới các chân đế, tất cả đều do vua Sa-lô-môn làm cho đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, chứa nhiều đồng đến nỗi không ai cân nổi.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 25:16 with the twelve bronze bulls added
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 25:16 names the two pillars, the Sea and the stands. Jeremiah adds the twelve bronze bulls and says "King Solomon". The bulls held up the Sea (1 Kings 7:25). Kings says that King Ahaz had taken the Sea down from the bulls and set it on a stone base (2 Kings 16:17), which may be why Kings does not name them here.

decisions.choice: under the stands: the Hebrew as it stands
alternatives: the twelve bronze bulls that were under the Sea
the twelve bronze bulls that were underneath, and the stands
decisions.reason: The bulls stood under the Sea, not under the stands (1 Kings 7:25). The Hebrew may mean "the bulls that were underneath, and the stands", with the stands listed separately as in 2 Kings 25:16, or a word may have been lost. As far as is known from general knowledge, the Greek reads "under the sea". The Hebrew wording is kept.

decisions.choice: there was no weight: it was too much to weigh
decisions.reason: The words repeat 1 Kings 7:47, where Solomon left the bronze unweighed because there was so much of it. What was too great to weigh when the temple was built is now carried away.

decisions.choice: all made by King Solomon (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Which King Solomon had made" most likely covers everything listed, not only the stands; Readable says "all made by" to show it. Readable leaves out "one" with the Sea.

decisions.choice: los doce bueyes de bronce que estaban debajo de las basas
decisions.reason: Only Jeremiah names the twelve bronze bulls here; the bulls stood under the Sea (1 Kings 7:25), and the Hebrew's "under the stands" is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: "mafahali kumi na wawili wa shaba" added to the wording of 2 Kings 25:16
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here names the twelve bronze bulls, which 2 Kings leaves out; the rest keeps the 2 Kings wording.

source.text: וְהָעַמּוּדִ֗ים שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה אַמָּה֙ קוֹמַת֙ הָעַמֻּ֣ד הָאֶחָ֔ד וְח֛וּט שְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה אַמָּ֖ה יְסֻבֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָבְי֛וֹ אַרְבַּ֥ע אַצְבָּע֖וֹת נָבֽוּב׃

records.literal_gloss: And the pillars, eighteen cubit[s] [was the] height of the pillar the one, and a line of twelve cubit[s] went around it, and its thickness [was] four fingers, hollow.

en.L: And the pillars: eighteen cubits [was] the height of the one pillar, and a line of twelve cubits went around it, and its thickness [was] four fingers; [it was] hollow.
en.B: As for the pillars, each pillar was {{units:about 27 feet|eighteen cubits}} high, and it took a line of {{units:about 18 feet|twelve cubits}} to go around it. Its metal was {{units:about 3 inches|four fingers}} thick, and it was hollow.
en.R: Each pillar was {{units:about 27 feet|eighteen cubits}} tall and {{units:about 18 feet|twelve cubits}} around. It was hollow, and its bronze was {{units:about 3 inches|four fingers}} thick.

es.L: Y las columnas: dieciocho codos [era] la altura de una columna, y un cordón de doce codos la rodeaba, y su grueso [era] de cuatro dedos; [era] hueca.
es.B: En cuanto a las columnas, cada una medía {{units:unos 8,10 metros|dieciocho codos}} de alto, y se necesitaba un cordón de {{units:unos 5,4 metros|doce codos}} para rodearla. Su metal tenía {{units:unos 7,5 centímetros|cuatro dedos}} de grueso, y era hueca.
es.R: Cada columna medía {{units:unos 8,10 metros|dieciocho codos}} de alto y {{units:unos 5,4 metros|doce codos}} de contorno. Era hueca, y su bronce tenía {{units:unos 7,5 centímetros|cuatro dedos}} de grueso.

fr.L: Et les colonnes : dix-huit coudées [était] la hauteur d’une colonne, et un cordeau de douze coudées en faisait le tour, et son épaisseur [était] de quatre doigts ; [elle était] creuse.
fr.B: Quant aux colonnes, chacune mesurait {{units:environ 8 mètres|dix-huit coudées}} de haut, et il fallait un cordeau de {{units:environ 5,40 mètres|douze coudées}} pour en faire le tour. Son métal avait {{units:environ 7 centimètres|quatre doigts}} d’épaisseur, et elle était creuse.
fr.R: Chaque colonne mesurait {{units:environ 8 mètres|dix-huit coudées}} de haut et {{units:environ 5,40 mètres|douze coudées}} de tour. Elle était creuse, et son bronze avait {{units:environ 7 centimètres|quatre doigts}} d’épaisseur.

sw.L: Na nguzo: urefu wa nguzo moja [ulikuwa] dhiraa kumi na nane, na uzi wa dhiraa kumi na mbili uliizunguka, na unene wake [ulikuwa] vidole vinne; [ilikuwa] na uvungu ndani.
sw.B: Kuhusu nguzo, kila nguzo ilikuwa na urefu wa {{units:karibu mita 8|dhiraa kumi na nane}}, na ilihitaji kamba ya {{units:karibu mita 5.4|dhiraa kumi na mbili}} kuizunguka. Unene wa shaba yake ulikuwa {{units:karibu sentimita 7.5|vidole vinne}}, nayo ilikuwa na uvungu ndani.
sw.R: Kila nguzo ilikuwa na urefu wa {{units:karibu mita 8|dhiraa kumi na nane}} na mzingo wa {{units:karibu mita 5.4|dhiraa kumi na mbili}}. Ilikuwa na uvungu ndani, na shaba yake ilikuwa na unene wa {{units:karibu sentimita 7.5|vidole vinne}}.

vi.L: Còn các cây trụ: chiều cao của một cây trụ [là] mười tám cu-đê, một sợi dây mười hai cu-đê đo vòng quanh nó, và bề dày của nó [là] bốn ngón tay; [nó] rỗng ruột.
vi.B: Còn các cây trụ, mỗi cây trụ cao {{units:8,1 m|mười tám cu-đê}}, và phải dùng một sợi dây dài {{units:5,4 m|mười hai cu-đê}} mới đo được vòng quanh. Kim loại dày {{units:7,5 cm|bốn ngón tay}}, và trụ rỗng ruột.
vi.R: Mỗi cây trụ cao {{units:8,1 m|mười tám cu-đê}} và chu vi {{units:5,4 m|mười hai cu-đê}}. Trụ rỗng ruột, và lớp đồng dày {{units:7,5 cm|bốn ngón tay}}.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 25:17 and 1 Kings 7:15
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 25:17 gives only the height, eighteen cubits. Jeremiah adds the measure around, twelve cubits, as 1 Kings 7:15 has it, and the thickness of the metal and that the pillars were hollow, which no other passage says.

decisions.choice: the height of the one pillar: of each pillar
decisions.reason: "The one pillar" means each of the two; the next verse says the second was like it (1 Kings 7:15).

decisions.choice: four fingers: about three inches
decisions.reason: A finger's breadth was the smallest measure of length, a quarter of a handbreadth. The pillars were cast as hollow bronze columns with walls about three inches thick.

decisions.choice: modern measures with the cubits and fingers as the alternative (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:15, a cubit is about 18 inches; four fingers are about 3 inches. Literal keeps the Hebrew units. Readable puts "hollow" before the thickness so the sentence reads more easily.

decisions.choice: {{units:unos 8,10 metros|dieciocho codos}} and the other measures
decisions.reason: Modern measures by default, with the cubits and fingers as the alternative, as in 2 Kings 25:17; Literal keeps the original units.

decisions.choice: units spans with metres and centimetres by default ("karibu mita 8") and the cubits and fingers as the alternative ("dhiraa kumi na nane")
alternatives: feet and inches as in the English
decisions.reason: The Swahili units setting is metric, as in 2 Kings 25:17; Literal keeps the original measures.

decisions.choice: metric measures, with the cubits and fingers as the alternative (a cubit of about 45 cm, as 2 Kings 25:17)
decisions.reason: French readers use the metric system; Literal keeps the original units, as the English does.

decisions.choice: metric measures by default, with the cubits and fingers as the alternative
decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 25:17 in Vietnamese: metric by default with the cubit at 45 cm and the finger at about 1.9 cm, the original unit as the alternative; Literal keeps cubits and fingers.

source.text: וְכֹתֶ֨רֶת עָלָ֜יו נְחֹ֗שֶׁת וְקוֹמַ֨ת הַכֹּתֶ֥רֶת הָאַחַת֮ חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּוֹת֒ וּשְׂבָכָ֨ה וְרִמּוֹנִ֧ים עַֽל־הַכּוֹתֶ֛רֶת סָבִ֖יב הַכֹּ֣ל נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְכָאֵ֛לֶּה לַֽעַמּ֥וּד הַשֵּׁנִ֖י וְרִמּוֹנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And a capital on it [of] bronze, and [the] height of the capital the one five cubits, and a network and pomegranates on the capital all around, the whole [of] bronze; and like these [was] to the pillar the second, and pomegranates.

en.L: And on it [was] a capital of bronze; and the height of the one capital [was] five cubits, and a network and pomegranates [were] on the capital all around, all of bronze; and the second pillar [had] the like, and pomegranates.
en.B: On top of it was a bronze capital. The capital was {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} high, with a network and pomegranates all around it, all of bronze. The second pillar, with its pomegranates, was the same.
en.R: It had a bronze top, called a capital, that was {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} tall. All around the capital was a net of lattice work with pomegranates on it, all made of bronze. The second pillar, with its pomegranates, was just the same.

es.L: Y sobre ella [había] un capitel de bronce; y la altura de un capitel [era] de cinco codos, y una red y granadas [había] sobre el capitel alrededor, todo de bronce; y semejante [tenía] la segunda columna, y granadas.
es.B: Encima tenía un capitel de bronce. El capitel medía {{units:unos 2,25 metros|cinco codos}} de alto, con una red y granadas alrededor, todo de bronce. La segunda columna, con sus granadas, era igual.
es.R: Tenía encima una pieza de bronce, llamada capitel, que medía {{units:unos 2,25 metros|cinco codos}} de alto. Alrededor del capitel había una red de bronce con granadas, todo hecho de bronce. La segunda columna, con sus granadas, era igual.

fr.L: Et sur elle [il y avait] un chapiteau de bronze ; et la hauteur d’un chapiteau [était] de cinq coudées, et un treillis et des grenades [étaient] sur le chapiteau tout autour, le tout de bronze ; et la seconde colonne [avait] la même chose, et des grenades.
fr.B: Elle portait un chapiteau de bronze. Le chapiteau avait {{units:environ 2,25 mètres|cinq coudées}} de haut, avec un treillis et des grenades tout autour, le tout en bronze. La seconde colonne, avec ses grenades, était semblable.
fr.R: Elle avait au sommet une pièce de bronze, appelée chapiteau, haute de {{units:environ 2,25 mètres|cinq coudées}}. Tout autour du chapiteau, il y avait un filet en treillis décoré de grenades, le tout en bronze. La seconde colonne, avec ses grenades, était exactement pareille.

sw.L: Na juu yake [kulikuwa na] kichwa cha shaba; na urefu wa kichwa kimoja [ulikuwa] dhiraa tano, na wavu na makomamanga [yalikuwa] juu ya kichwa pande zote, yote ya shaba; na nguzo ya pili [ilikuwa na] mfano wa hayo, na makomamanga.
sw.B: Juu yake kulikuwa na kichwa cha shaba. Kichwa hicho kilikuwa na urefu wa {{units:karibu mita 2.3|dhiraa tano}}, chenye wavu na makomamanga pande zote, vyote vya shaba. Nguzo ya pili, pamoja na makomamanga yake, ilikuwa vivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Juu yake kulikuwa na kipande cha shaba kilichoitwa kichwa, chenye urefu wa {{units:karibu mita 2.3|dhiraa tano}}. Kuzunguka kichwa hicho kulikuwa na wavu wa kazi ya kusuka wenye makomamanga, vyote vya shaba. Nguzo ya pili, pamoja na makomamanga yake, ilikuwa sawasawa kabisa.

vi.L: Trên đó [có] một đầu trụ bằng đồng; chiều cao của một đầu trụ [là] năm cu-đê, có lưới và trái lựu chung quanh đầu trụ, tất cả bằng đồng; cây trụ thứ hai cũng [có] như vậy, với trái lựu.
vi.B: Trên đỉnh trụ có đầu trụ bằng đồng. Đầu trụ cao {{units:2,25 m|năm cu-đê}}, chung quanh có lưới và trái lựu, tất cả đều bằng đồng. Cây trụ thứ hai, với các trái lựu của nó, cũng giống như vậy.
vi.R: Trên đỉnh trụ có một phần đầu bằng đồng, gọi là đầu trụ, cao {{units:2,25 m|năm cu-đê}}. Chung quanh đầu trụ có một tấm lưới đan với những trái lựu, tất cả đều bằng đồng. Cây trụ thứ hai, với các trái lựu của nó, cũng giống hệt như vậy.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 25:17: three cubits there, five here
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 25:17 gives the capital a height of three cubits; Jeremiah gives five, as 1 Kings 7:16 and 2 Chronicles 3:15 do. Kings may have a copying error, or may measure only part of the capital. Kings also ends "with the network", where Jeremiah ends "and pomegranates".

decisions.choice: network and pomegranates: a lattice with bronze fruit
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:17-20, the network is a lattice of crossing bands around the capital, and the pomegranates are bronze ornaments in rows on it.

decisions.choice: like these to the second pillar: the second was the same
decisions.reason: Everything said of the first pillar holds for the second; "and pomegranates" names the part described most fully in the next verse.

decisions.choice: a bronze top, called a capital (Readable); modern measure (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:17, Readable explains "capital"; five cubits are about 7 1/2 feet, as in 1 Kings 7:16.

decisions.choice: cinco codos
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's Hebrew gives the capital five cubits, as 1 Kings 7:16, where 2 Kings 25:17 has three.

decisions.choice: "dhiraa tano" (five cubits) where 2 Kings 25:17 has three
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse gives a different height for the capital; the Swahili follows it.

decisions.choice: năm cu-đê (five cubits)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah gives the capital five cubits, where 2 Kings 25:17 has three; Vietnamese follows the Hebrew here.

source.text: וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ הָֽרִמֹּנִ֔ים תִּשְׁעִ֥ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֖ה ר֑וּחָה כָּל־הָרִמּוֹנִ֥ים מֵאָ֛ה עַל־הַשְּׂבָכָ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And were the pomegranates ninety and six toward [the] wind; all the pomegranates [were a] hundred on the network all around.

en.L: And the pomegranates were ninety-six on the sides; all the pomegranates [were] a hundred on the network all around.
en.B: There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; in all there were a hundred pomegranates on the network all around.
en.R: There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides. Altogether a hundred pomegranates went around the network.

es.L: Y había noventa y seis granadas hacia los lados; todas las granadas [eran] cien sobre la red alrededor.
es.B: Había noventa y seis granadas en los lados; en total había cien granadas sobre la red, alrededor.
es.R: Había noventa y seis granadas en los lados. En total, cien granadas rodeaban la red.

fr.L: Et les grenades étaient quatre-vingt-seize sur les côtés ; toutes les grenades [étaient] cent sur le treillis tout autour.
fr.B: Il y avait quatre-vingt-seize grenades sur les côtés ; en tout, il y avait cent grenades sur le treillis tout autour.
fr.R: Il y avait quatre-vingt-seize grenades sur les côtés. En tout, cent grenades faisaient le tour du treillis.

sw.L: Na makomamanga yalikuwa tisini na sita pembeni; makomamanga yote [yalikuwa] mia moja juu ya wavu pande zote.
sw.B: Kulikuwa na makomamanga tisini na sita pembeni; kwa jumla kulikuwa na makomamanga mia moja juu ya wavu pande zote.
sw.R: Kulikuwa na makomamanga tisini na sita pembeni. Kwa jumla makomamanga mia moja yalizunguka wavu.

vi.L: Có chín mươi sáu trái lựu ở các mặt bên; tất cả trái lựu trên lưới chung quanh [là] một trăm.
vi.B: Có chín mươi sáu trái lựu ở các mặt bên; tổng cộng có một trăm trái lựu trên tấm lưới chung quanh.
vi.R: Có chín mươi sáu trái lựu ở các mặt bên. Tất cả có một trăm trái lựu bao quanh tấm lưới.

decisions.choice: on the sides: literally "toward the wind"
decisions.reason: The phrase, used only here, seems to mean the sides facing outward, toward the four winds. Perhaps ninety-six could be seen from the sides and four more were hidden or stood at the corners, making a hundred in each row. The exact sense is not known.

decisions.choice: a hundred in a row: 1 Kings 7:20, 42
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:20 speaks of two hundred pomegranates in rows around each capital, and 1 Kings 7:42 of four hundred for the two networks, two rows on each. That fits a hundred in each row. 2 Kings 25 gives no numbers.

decisions.choice: on the sides
decisions.reason: All levels say "on the sides" for the rare phrase "toward the wind", without settling what it means (see the meaning decision).

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח רַב־טַבָּחִ֗ים אֶת־שְׂרָיָה֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְאֶת־צְפַנְיָ֖ה כֹּהֵ֣ן הַמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה וְאֶת־שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת שֹׁמְרֵ֥י הַסַּֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And took [the] chief of [the] guards Seraiah [the] priest of the head, and Zephaniah [the] priest of the second [rank], and [the] three keepers of the threshold.

en.L: And the chief of the guard took Seraiah the head priest and Zephaniah the second priest and the three keepers of the threshold.
en.B: The captain of the guard also seized Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next to him, and the three doorkeepers.
en.R: The commander of the guard also arrested Seraiah the high priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank, and the three men who guarded the temple entrance.

es.L: Y el jefe de la guardia tomó a Seraías, el sacerdote principal, y a Sofonías, el segundo sacerdote, y a los tres guardianes del umbral.
es.B: El capitán de la guardia también apresó a Seraías, el sacerdote principal, a Sofonías, el sacerdote que le seguía en rango, y a los tres porteros.
es.R: El comandante de la guardia también arrestó a Seraías, el sumo sacerdote, a Sofonías, el sacerdote que le seguía en rango, y a los tres hombres que cuidaban la entrada del templo.

fr.L: Et le chef des gardes prit Seraya le prêtre en chef, et Sophonie le second prêtre, et les trois gardiens du seuil.
fr.B: Le commandant de la garde prit aussi Seraya, le prêtre en chef, Sophonie, le prêtre en second, et les trois gardiens du seuil.
fr.R: Le chef de la garde a aussi arrêté Seraya, le grand prêtre, Sophonie, le prêtre qui venait après lui, et les trois hommes qui gardaient l’entrée du temple.

sw.L: Naye mkuu wa walinzi akamchukua Seraya kuhani mkuu na Sefania kuhani wa pili, na walinzi watatu wa kizingiti.
sw.B: Kamanda wa walinzi alimkamata pia Seraya kuhani mkuu, Sefania kuhani aliyefuata kwa cheo, na mabawabu watatu.
sw.R: Kamanda wa walinzi alimkamata pia Seraya kuhani mkuu, Sefania kuhani aliyefuata kwa cheo, na watu watatu waliolinda mlango wa hekalu.

vi.L: Quan chỉ huy vệ binh bắt Sê-ra-gia, thầy tế lễ đứng đầu, Sô-phô-ni, thầy tế lễ bậc thứ hai, và ba người giữ ngưỡng cửa.
vi.B: Quan chỉ huy đội cận vệ cũng bắt Sê-ra-gia, thầy tế lễ cả, Sô-phô-ni, thầy tế lễ phó, và ba người giữ cửa.
vi.R: Người chỉ huy đội cận vệ cũng bắt giữ Sê-ra-gia, thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm, Sô-phô-ni, thầy tế lễ bậc kế tiếp, và ba người canh giữ lối vào đền thờ.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 25:18
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 2 Kings 25:18 apart from a shorter spelling of Zephaniah's name and "the" before "second", and the wording follows it.

decisions.choice: Seraiah the head priest: the high priest
decisions.reason: "The head priest" is the leading priest of the temple (2 Chronicles 19:11). Seraiah was the grandson of Hilkiah, the high priest under Josiah, and an ancestor of Ezra (1 Chronicles 5:39-41; Ezra 7:1). He is not the Seraiah son of Neriah of 51:59.

decisions.choice: Zephaniah the second priest: the high priest's deputy
decisions.reason: The priest "of second rank" was next after the high priest (2 Kings 23:4). Zephaniah son of Maaseiah carried messages between King Zedekiah and Jeremiah (21:1; 29:25-29; 37:3).

decisions.choice: the keepers of the threshold: senior temple officers
decisions.reason: They guarded the entrances of the temple and received the money brought in (2 Kings 12:10; 22:4). Jeremiah 35:4 names one of them, Maaseiah son of Shallum.

decisions.choice: doorkeepers (Balanced); the men who guarded the temple entrance (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:18, Balanced and Readable explain the titles, and Readable says "arrested" for "took".

source.text: וּמִן־הָעִ֡יר לָקַח֩ סָרִ֨יס אֶחָ֜ד אֲֽשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה פָקִ֣יד׀עַל־אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְשִׁבְעָ֨ה אֲנָשִׁ֜ים מֵרֹאֵ֤י פְנֵי־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצְא֣וּ בָעִ֔יר וְאֵ֗ת סֹפֵר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֔א הַמַּצְבִּ֖א אֶת־עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מֵעַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And from the city he took one official who had been overseer over [the] men of the war, and seven men of [those] seeing [the] face of the king who were found in the city, and [the] scribe of [the] commander of the army, the one mustering the people of the land, and sixty men of [the] people of the land, the ones found in [the] midst of the city.

en.L: And from the city he took one eunuch who had been the overseer over the men of war, and seven men of those who saw the face of the king, who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city.
en.B: From the city he took a court officer who had been in charge of the soldiers, seven of the king's advisers who were found in the city, the secretary of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land for war, and sixty of the people of the land who were still in the city.
en.R: From the city he also took the palace official in charge of the soldiers and seven of the king's close advisers who were still in the city. He took the army commander's secretary, who called up the men of the land to serve in the army. He also took sixty of those men who were still in the city.

es.L: Y de la ciudad tomó a un eunuco que era el encargado de los hombres de guerra, y a siete hombres de los que veían el rostro del rey que se hallaron en la ciudad, y al escriba del jefe del ejército, que reclutaba al pueblo de la tierra, y a sesenta hombres del pueblo de la tierra que se hallaron en medio de la ciudad.
es.B: De la ciudad tomó a un funcionario que había estado a cargo de los soldados, a siete de los consejeros del rey que se encontraban en la ciudad, al secretario del jefe del ejército, que reclutaba para la guerra al pueblo de la tierra, y a sesenta hombres del pueblo de la tierra que todavía estaban en la ciudad.
es.R: De la ciudad también tomó al oficial encargado de los soldados y a siete de los consejeros más cercanos del rey que todavía estaban en la ciudad. Tomó al secretario del jefe del ejército, que llamaba a los hombres del país a servir en el ejército. También tomó a sesenta de esos hombres que todavía estaban en la ciudad.

fr.L: Et de la ville il prit un eunuque qui était préposé aux hommes de guerre, et sept hommes de ceux qui voyaient la face du roi, qui se trouvaient dans la ville, et le secrétaire du chef de l’armée, qui recrutait le peuple du pays, et soixante hommes du peuple du pays qui se trouvaient au milieu de la ville.
fr.B: Il prit dans la ville un haut fonctionnaire qui commandait les soldats, sept des conseillers du roi qu’on trouva dans la ville, le secrétaire du chef de l’armée, qui enrôlait le peuple du pays pour la guerre, et soixante hommes du peuple du pays qui se trouvaient encore dans la ville.
fr.R: Dans la ville, il a aussi pris le fonctionnaire du palais qui commandait les soldats, et sept des proches conseillers du roi qui étaient encore là. Il a pris le secrétaire du chef de l’armée, qui appelait les hommes du pays à servir dans l’armée. Il a aussi pris soixante de ces hommes qui étaient encore dans la ville.

sw.L: Na kutoka mjini akamchukua towashi mmoja aliyekuwa msimamizi juu ya watu wa vita, na watu saba wa wale walioona uso wa mfalme, walioonekana mjini, na mwandishi wa jemadari wa jeshi, aliyewaandikisha watu wa nchi, na watu sitini wa watu wa nchi walioonekana katikati ya mji.
sw.B: Kutoka mjini alimchukua afisa mmoja aliyekuwa msimamizi wa askari, washauri saba wa mfalme walioonekana mjini, katibu wa mkuu wa jeshi, aliyewaandikisha watu wa nchi kwenda vitani, na watu sitini wa watu wa nchi waliokuwa bado mjini.
sw.R: Kutoka mjini alimchukua pia afisa aliyesimamia askari na washauri saba wa karibu wa mfalme waliokuwa bado mjini. Alimchukua katibu wa mkuu wa jeshi, aliyewaita watu wa nchi kujiunga na jeshi. Pia aliwachukua watu sitini wa hao waliokuwa bado mjini.

vi.L: Từ trong thành hắn bắt một hoạn quan là người được giao cai quản quân lính, bảy người trong số những người được thấy mặt vua còn ở trong thành, viên thư ký của tướng chỉ huy quân đội, là người tuyển mộ dân trong xứ, và sáu mươi người trong dân của xứ còn ở giữa thành.
vi.B: Từ trong thành hắn bắt một triều thần đã chỉ huy quân lính, bảy cố vấn của vua còn ở trong thành, viên thư ký của tướng chỉ huy quân đội, là người lo tuyển mộ dân trong xứ ra trận, và sáu mươi người dân trong xứ còn ở trong thành.
vi.R: Từ trong thành hắn cũng bắt viên quan chỉ huy quân lính và bảy cố vấn thân cận của vua còn ở trong thành. Hắn bắt viên thư ký của tướng chỉ huy quân đội, là người gọi đàn ông trong xứ nhập ngũ. Hắn cũng bắt sáu mươi người trong số những người ấy còn ở trong thành.

decisions.choice: seven of the king's advisers here; five in 2 Kings 25:19
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Kings 25:19, but where Kings has five men "who saw the face of the king", Jeremiah has seven. One number may have been miscopied; the Hebrew of each book is followed. Jeremiah also says the officer "had been" in charge, and "in the midst of the city" for "in the city".

decisions.choice: a royal officer
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:19, the word can mean a eunuch, but it was also a title for a high officer of the king (Genesis 37:36). Here it is a military officer in command of the soldiers.

decisions.choice: those who saw the face of the king: his closest advisers
decisions.reason: Only trusted counselors were allowed into the king's presence (Esther 1:14).

decisions.choice: the scribe of the commander of the army
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's Hebrew reads plainly "the scribe of the commander of the army", the secretary who kept the lists for calling men up. 2 Kings 25:19 can be read "the scribe, the commander of the army"; Jeremiah settles the sense.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the landholding men of Judah
decisions.reason: Here the phrase names the citizens of Judah who held land and were called up to fight (34:19; 2 Kings 23:30). The sixty were probably leading men of that class.

decisions.choice: the king's advisers; mustered ... for war (Balanced); called up ... to serve in the army (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:19, Balanced and Readable say who "those who saw the king's face" were and what mustering was for. Readable splits the list into three sentences.

decisions.choice: eunuch (Literal); court officer (Balanced); palace official (Readable)
decisions.reason: As set for this word in Jeremiah and in 2 Kings 24:12, Literal keeps "eunuch", and Balanced and Readable say "court officer" and "palace official" (m2). 2 Kings 25:19 has "official" and "officer" here; this verse follows the wording set for Jeremiah instead.

decisions.choice: siete
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's Hebrew has seven of the king's advisers where 2 Kings 25:19 has five.

decisions.choice: "watu saba" (seven) where 2 Kings 25:19 has five
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse counts seven of the king's advisers; the rest keeps the 2 Kings wording.

decisions.choice: bảy người (seven)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah names seven of the king's advisers where 2 Kings 25:19 names five; the rest of the verse reuses the Kings wording.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אוֹתָ֔ם נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן רַב־טַבָּחִ֑ים וַיֹּ֧לֶךְ אוֹתָ֛ם אֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל רִבְלָֽתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took them Nebuzaradan chief of [the] guards, and brought them to [the] king of Babylon to Riblah.

en.L: And Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon, to Riblah.
en.B: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard led them away to Riblah and brought them before the king of Babylon.
en.R: Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took them all to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

es.L: Y Nabuzaradán, jefe de la guardia, los tomó y los llevó al rey de Babilonia, a Ribla.
es.B: Nabuzaradán, capitán de la guardia, se los llevó a Ribla y los presentó ante el rey de Babilonia.
es.R: Nabuzaradán, el comandante de la guardia, los llevó a todos ante el rey de Babilonia, en Ribla.

fr.L: Et Nebouzaradân, chef des gardes, les prit et les conduisit vers le roi de Babylone, à Ribla.
fr.B: Nebouzaradân, le commandant de la garde, les emmena à Ribla et les amena devant le roi de Babylone.
fr.R: Nebouzaradân, le chef de la garde, les a tous emmenés au roi de Babylone, à Ribla.

sw.L: Naye Nebuzaradani mkuu wa walinzi akawachukua, akawaleta kwa mfalme wa Babeli huko Ribla.
sw.B: Nebuzaradani kamanda wa walinzi aliwachukua mpaka Ribla, akawaleta mbele ya mfalme wa Babeli.
sw.R: Nebuzaradani, kamanda wa walinzi, aliwapeleka wote kwa mfalme wa Babeli huko Ribla.

vi.L: Nê-bu-xa-a-đan, quan chỉ huy vệ binh, bắt họ và đem họ đến vua Ba-by-lôn tại Ríp-la.
vi.B: Nê-bu-xa-a-đan, quan chỉ huy đội cận vệ, giải họ đến Ríp-la, trình vua Ba-by-lôn.
vi.R: Nê-bu-xa-a-đan, người chỉ huy đội cận vệ, đem tất cả họ đến vua Ba-by-lôn tại Ríp-la.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 25:20
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is the same as 2 Kings 25:20, and the wording follows it.

decisions.choice: Riblah: Nebuchadrezzar's camp in Syria
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, where Zedekiah had been judged.

source.text: וַיַּכֶּ֣ה אוֹתָם֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֧ל וַיְמִתֵ֛ם בְּרִבְלָ֖ה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֑ת וַיִּ֥גֶל יְהוּדָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And struck them [the] king of Babylon and put them to death at Riblah in [the] land of Hamath. And went into exile Judah from upon its land.

en.L: And the king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.
en.B: The king of Babylon had them struck down and executed at Riblah, in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile, away from its own land.
en.R: The king of Babylon had them killed there at Riblah, in the land of Hamath. So the people of Judah were taken away from their land as captives.

es.L: Y el rey de Babilonia los hirió y les dio muerte en Ribla, en la tierra de Hamat. Así fue llevado cautivo Judá de sobre su tierra.
es.B: El rey de Babilonia los hizo matar y ejecutar en Ribla, en la tierra de Hamat. Así Judá fue llevado al destierro, lejos de su propia tierra.
es.R: El rey de Babilonia los mandó matar allí, en Ribla, en la tierra de Hamat. Así la gente de Judá fue llevada prisionera lejos de su tierra.

fr.L: Et le roi de Babylone les frappa et les fit mourir à Ribla, au pays de Hamath. Et Juda fut déporté loin de sa terre.
fr.B: Le roi de Babylone les fit frapper et exécuter à Ribla, au pays de Hamath. Ainsi Juda fut emmené en exil, loin de sa terre.
fr.R: Le roi de Babylone les a fait tuer là, à Ribla, au pays de Hamath. Ainsi, le peuple de Juda a été emmené loin de son pays comme prisonnier.

sw.L: Naye mfalme wa Babeli akawapiga, akawaua huko Ribla katika nchi ya Hamathi. Basi Yuda akahamishwa kutoka katika nchi yake.
sw.B: Mfalme wa Babeli aliamuru wapigwe na kuuawa huko Ribla, katika nchi ya Hamathi. Basi Yuda walichukuliwa uhamishoni, mbali na nchi yao wenyewe.
sw.R: Mfalme wa Babeli aliamuru wauawe huko Ribla, katika nchi ya Hamathi. Basi watu wa Yuda walichukuliwa mateka kutoka katika nchi yao.

vi.L: Vua Ba-by-lôn đánh họ và giết họ tại Ríp-la trong xứ Ha-mát. Vậy Giu-đa bị lưu đày khỏi đất mình.
vi.B: Vua Ba-by-lôn cho đánh giết họ tại Ríp-la, trong xứ Ha-mát. Vậy Giu-đa bị lưu đày khỏi đất của mình.
vi.R: Vua Ba-by-lôn cho giết họ tại Ríp-la, trong xứ Ha-mát. Vậy dân Giu-đa bị bắt đem khỏi đất mình làm tù binh.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 25:21; then the accounts part
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is the same as 2 Kings 25:21. Kings goes on to tell of Gedaliah, the governor left over the land, his murder and the flight to Egypt (2 Kings 25:22-26). Jeremiah leaves that out, having told it at length (40:7-43:7), and gives instead the numbers taken into exile (verses 28-30).

decisions.choice: Judah went into exile from its land
decisions.reason: The same words were said of the northern kingdom (2 Kings 17:23). Jeremiah had warned for forty years that the LORD would send Judah out of the land (1:13-16; 25:8-11).

decisions.choice: the people of Judah (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:21, Readable says "the people of Judah" for the nation, and "as captives" for going into exile.

source.text: זֶ֣ה הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶגְלָ֖ה נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֑ר בִּשְׁנַת־שֶׁ֕בַע יְהוּדִ֕ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is] the people whom exiled Nebuchadrezzar: in [the] year seven, Judeans three thousand and twenty and three.

en.L: This [is] the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Judeans.
en.B: These are the people Nebuchadrezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Judeans.
en.R: Here are the numbers of people Nebuchadrezzar took away as captives. In the seventh year that he was king, he took 3,023 people from Judah.

es.L: Este [es] el pueblo que Nabucodorosor llevó cautivo: en el año séptimo, 3 023 judíos.
es.B: Esta es la gente que Nabucodorosor llevó al destierro: en el año séptimo, 3 023 judíos.
es.R: Estos son los números de la gente que Nabucodorosor se llevó prisionera. En el séptimo año de su reinado, se llevó a 3 023 personas de Judá.

fr.L: Voici le peuple que Nabuchodonosor déporta : la septième année, trois mille vingt-trois Judéens.
fr.B: Voici le nombre des gens que Nabuchodonosor emmena en exil : la septième année, trois mille vingt-trois Judéens.
fr.R: Voici le nombre des gens que Nabuchodonosor a emmenés comme prisonniers. La septième année de son règne, il a emmené trois mille vingt-trois personnes de Juda.

sw.L: Hawa [ndio] watu ambao Nebukadreza aliwahamisha: katika mwaka wa saba, Wayahudi 3,023.

decisions.choice: verses 28-30 are part of the Hebrew text; the Greek lacks them
alternatives: leave out verses 28-30 with the Greek
decisions.reason: As far as is known from general knowledge, the Septuagint of Jeremiah does not have verses 28-30 and goes straight from verse 27 to the release of Jehoiachin (verse 31). 2 Kings 25 does not have them either. This translation follows the Hebrew (see the note at 1:1).

decisions.choice: the seventh year: the exile of Jehoiachin in 597 BC, with a smaller number than 2 Kings 24
alternatives: a deportation from the towns of Judah before Jehoiachin's surrender
decisions.reason: Nebuchadrezzar's seventh year is the year he took Jerusalem the first time and carried off King Jehoiachin (2 Kings 24:10-16). 2 Kings 24:12 calls it his eighth year, probably counting the year he came to the throne as his first; the two books count his reign in different ways. 2 Kings 24:14 says ten thousand were taken then, and 24:16 seven thousand fighting men and a thousand craftsmen, far more than 3,023. This list may count only the adult men, or only the people of one class or from certain towns, or it may come from a Babylonian record of a particular group. What it counted is not known.

decisions.choice: Judeans: people of Judah
decisions.reason: The word names the people of the kingdom of Judah, as in 32:12 and 40:11-12.

decisions.choice: this is the people: a list follows
decisions.reason: The words introduce the three numbers that follow in verses 28-30 and their total.

decisions.choice: the seventh year that he was king; he took (Readable)

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 25:27: the twenty-seventh day
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Kings 25:27, but Kings dates the release to the twenty-seventh of the month, not the twenty-fifth. The difference may come from copying, or from counting the order and the release separately. Jeremiah also adds "and brought him out", where Kings has only "from the house of imprisonment".

decisions.choice: lifted up the head: showed favor and released
decisions.reason: To lift up someone's head is to raise him from disgrace to favor, as Pharaoh lifted up the head of his cupbearer and brought him out of prison (Genesis 40:13, 20).

decisions.choice: Evil-Merodach: the Babylonian king Awel-Marduk
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:27, the name is the Hebrew form of Awel-Marduk, "man of Marduk", Nebuchadrezzar's son, who reigned for about two years. In Hebrew the first part sounds like the word for "foolish", which may be no more than the way the name was heard.

decisions.choice: Jehoiachin: the king Jeremiah also calls Jeconiah and Coniah
decisions.reason: The verse uses the form Jehoiachin, as Kings does. Elsewhere Jeremiah calls the same king Jeconiah (24:1; 27:20) and Coniah (22:24, 28), and said that no son of his would sit on David's throne (22:30).

decisions.choice: the thirty-seventh year: about 561 BC
decisions.reason: Jehoiachin was taken to Babylon at eighteen, in 597 BC (2 Kings 24:8-15). Thirty-seven years later, in the year Evil-Merodach came to the throne, he was about fifty-five. The twelfth month falls at the end of winter.

decisions.choice: showed favor ... and brought him out (Balanced); showed Jehoiachin favor (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:27, Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom instead of the picture of lifting the head, and say "in the year he became king" for "in the year of his reign". Readable splits the date into short sentences. Balanced says "the thirty-seventh year after Jehoiachin ... went into exile" for "the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin".

decisions.choice: a los veinticinco [días]; Joaquín
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's Hebrew has the twenty-fifth day where 2 Kings 25:27 has the twenty-seventh; the king's name keeps the form Jehoiachin (Joaquín), as there.

decisions.choice: "siku ya ishirini na tano" (the 25th) where 2 Kings 25:27 has the 27th
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse gives a different day; the rest keeps the 2 Kings wording, including "akakiinua kichwa" at Literal.

decisions.choice: ngày hai mươi lăm (the twenty-fifth)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah has the twenty-fifth day where 2 Kings 25:27 has the twenty-seventh; Vietnamese follows the Hebrew of each, and keeps the Kings wording otherwise.

decisions.choice: the seat above the other kings: first place among the captive kings
decisions.reason: The Babylonian kings kept rulers of conquered lands at their court. Jehoiachin was given a seat higher than all of them, a public sign of honor.

source.text: וְשִׁנָּ֕ה אֵ֖ת בִּגְדֵ֣י כִלְא֑וֹ וְאָכַ֨ל לֶ֧חֶם לְפָנָ֛יו תָּמִ֖יד כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he changed [the] clothes of his imprisonment, and he ate bread before him continually all [the] days of his life.

en.L: And he changed his prison clothes, and he ate bread continually before him all the days of his life.
en.B: So Jehoiachin put off his prison clothes, and for the rest of his life he ate regularly at the king's table.
en.R: Jehoiachin no longer had to wear prison clothes. For the rest of his life he ate his meals at the king's table.

es.L: Y cambió sus vestidos de prisión, y comió pan continuamente delante de él todos los días de su vida.
es.B: Así Joaquín se quitó la ropa de prisionero, y por el resto de su vida comió siempre a la mesa del rey.
es.R: Joaquín ya no tuvo que usar ropa de prisionero. Por el resto de su vida comió a la mesa del rey.

fr.L: Et il changea ses vêtements de prison, et il mangea le pain continuellement devant lui, tous les jours de sa vie.
fr.B: Joïakin quitta ses vêtements de prisonnier, et tout le reste de sa vie il mangea régulièrement à la table du roi.
fr.R: Joïakin n’a plus eu à porter des vêtements de prisonnier. Jusqu’à la fin de sa vie, il a pris ses repas à la table du roi.

sw.L: Naye akabadilisha mavazi yake ya kifungo, akala chakula daima mbele yake siku zote za maisha yake.
sw.B: Basi Yehoyakini akayavua mavazi yake ya gerezani, na kwa maisha yake yote yaliyobaki akala daima mezani pa mfalme.
sw.R: Yehoyakini hakuvaa tena mavazi ya gerezani. Kwa maisha yake yote yaliyobaki alikula chakula chake mezani pa mfalme.

vi.L: Ông thay áo tù, và ông ăn bánh thường xuyên trước mặt vua ấy mọi ngày trong đời ông.
vi.B: Vậy Giê-hô-gia-kin cởi bỏ áo tù, và suốt quãng đời còn lại ông thường xuyên ăn tại bàn vua.
vi.R: Giê-hô-gia-kin không còn phải mặc áo tù nữa. Suốt quãng đời còn lại, ông được ăn uống tại bàn của vua.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 25:29
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 2 Kings 25:29 with "continually" and "before him" in the other order, and the wording follows it.

decisions.choice: he changed: Jehoiachin changed his clothes
decisions.reason: The subject is most likely Jehoiachin, who put off his prison clothes; it could also be the king, who had them changed. Either way his time as a prisoner was over.

decisions.choice: ate bread before him: ate at the king's table
decisions.reason: To eat at the king's table was a mark of honor and of provision for life, as David gave Jonathan's son Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9:7, 13).

decisions.choice: Jehoiachin; at the king's table (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:29, Balanced and Readable name Jehoiachin and say "at the king's table" for "before him".

source.text: וַאֲרֻחָת֗וֹ אֲרֻחַת֩ תָּמִ֨יד נִתְּנָה־לּ֜וֹ מֵאֵ֧ת מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל דְּבַר־י֥וֹם בְּיוֹמ֖וֹ עַד־י֣וֹם מוֹת֑וֹ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And his allowance, an allowance continual, was given to him from with [the] king of Babylon, [a] matter of [a] day in its day, until [the] day of his death, all [the] days of his life.

en.L: And his allowance, a regular allowance, was given to him by the king of Babylon, a day's portion each day, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.
en.B: And the king of Babylon gave him a regular allowance, a portion for each day, until the day he died, all the days of his life.
en.R: Every day the king of Babylon gave him what he needed for that day. This went on as long as he lived, until the day he died.

es.L: Y su ración, una ración continua, le fue dada de parte del rey de Babilonia, la porción de cada día en su día, hasta el día de su muerte, todos los días de su vida.
es.B: Y el rey de Babilonia le dio una ración fija, una porción para cada día, hasta el día de su muerte, todos los días de su vida.
es.R: Cada día el rey de Babilonia le daba lo que necesitaba para ese día. Así fue mientras vivió, hasta el día de su muerte.

fr.L: Et son entretien, un entretien continuel, lui fut donné de la part du roi de Babylone, la ration de chaque jour en son jour, jusqu’au jour de sa mort, tous les jours de sa vie.
fr.B: Et le roi de Babylone lui assura un entretien régulier, une portion pour chaque jour, jusqu’au jour de sa mort, tous les jours de sa vie.
fr.R: Chaque jour, le roi de Babylone lui donnait ce dont il avait besoin pour la journée. Cela a duré tant qu’il a vécu, jusqu’au jour de sa mort.

sw.L: Na posho lake, posho la daima, alipewa na mfalme wa Babeli, kiasi cha siku kwa siku yake, mpaka siku ya kufa kwake, siku zote za maisha yake.
sw.B: Naye mfalme wa Babeli akampa posho la daima, sehemu ya kila siku, mpaka siku alipokufa, siku zote za maisha yake.
sw.R: Kila siku mfalme wa Babeli alimpa mahitaji yake ya siku hiyo. Hivyo ndivyo ilivyokuwa maisha yake yote, mpaka siku alipokufa.

vi.L: Phần lương của ông, một phần lương thường xuyên, được vua Ba-by-lôn cấp cho ông, mỗi ngày một phần, cho đến ngày ông chết, mọi ngày trong đời ông.
vi.B: Vua Ba-by-lôn cấp cho ông một phần lương thường xuyên, mỗi ngày một phần, cho đến ngày ông qua đời, suốt đời ông.
vi.R: Mỗi ngày vua Ba-by-lôn cấp cho ông những gì ông cần dùng trong ngày ấy. Việc ấy kéo dài suốt cuộc đời ông, cho đến ngày ông qua đời.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 25:30 with "until the day of his death"
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Kings 25:30, but names "the king of Babylon" where Kings has "the king", and adds "until the day of his death". The same words closed the account of Zedekiah (verse 11): both kings of Judah ended their days in Babylon, one blind in prison, the other honored at the king's table.

decisions.choice: a day's portion each day: a daily share
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of a daily quota or ration (Exodus 5:13; 16:4). The king provided for him day by day.

decisions.choice: the allowance: royal rations
decisions.reason: Clay tablets from Nebuchadrezzar's palace in Babylon record rations of oil given to "Ya'ukin, king of the land of Yahud" and to his sons, which shows that Jehoiachin was already supplied by the court years earlier.

decisions.choice: an open ending: the book closes with David's heir alive in exile
decisions.reason: The book of Jeremiah does not end with the burning of the temple but with the king of David's line freed and honored in Babylon. Jeremiah had told the exiles to settle there and wait, for the LORD would bring them back after seventy years (29:4-14). The writer does not say what Jehoiachin's release means, but the ending leaves room for the hope the book has held out (23:5-6; 33:14-17).

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon gave him (Balanced, Readable); what he needed for that day (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:30, Balanced and Readable make the king the subject instead of the passive "was given". Readable explains the allowance and puts "as long as he lived" before "until the day he died" so that the two phrases do not repeat each other word for word.

decisions.choice: hasta el día de su muerte
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's Hebrew adds "until the day of his death" to the wording of 2 Kings 25:30.
